title: Rabbi Zeira bar Chanina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Niddah 3b for a passage in which he resolves a difficulty in the Gemara. Hyman suggests that he is called Ze’or or Ze’ir bar Chinena in the Jerusalem Talmud. In [Berakhot 5:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.5.1.4): “Ze’or bar Chinena said: one who lets blood from consecrated [animals] commits misappropriation”; also [Shabbat 7:2, 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.54), and there, [end of halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.4.3). In [Sanhedrin, beginning of chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.4.1.2), he reported in Rabbi Chanina’s name; in [Avodah Zarah 4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.5.2), in Rabbi Chananiah’s name (Rabbi Chanina, the Rabbis’ colleague).

And in [Terumot, end of ch. 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.8.4.13), it is related that once he was captured by bandits, and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Shemuel went to Zenobia the queen to intercede on his behalf, and through a miracle he was saved.

notes.text: [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1155&lang=en) cites [Niddah 50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.50b.14), where Rabbi Zeira bar Chanina answers a question about a bird that fell into a winepress. The named occurrence at Hyman’s 3b remains unverified. Ḥaveron de-rabbanan means “the Rabbis’ colleague.”

The linked Yerushalmi Berakhot has Ze’or bar Chinena giving the ruling about drawing blood from a consecrated animal. In [Bavli Berakhot 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.31a.9), Rav Huna gives a parallel in Rabbi Zeira’s name. The two Shabbat passages and Sanhedrin name Ze’ir bar Chinena reporting in Rabbi Chanina’s name. In Avodah Zarah the consulted text gives Rabbi Chanina where Hyman writes Rabbi Chananiah. Terumot has the rescue story and gives Safsufa as the place of capture.
